method: Each aircraft's next periodic servicing (50 FH) and phase inspection (150 FH) are projected from the FH flown since the last recorded one, at that aircraft's trailing 90-day utilisation rate. A phase inspection also covers the periodic servicing.

Planned package lengths are the midpoint of the configured ranges rounded up: 13 days for a phase inspection, 3 days for a periodic servicing. Packages are extended by whole days of bundled work at 16 man-hours per aircraft per day.
Each open recommendation's deadline is its due date, or the date its FH margin runs out at the trailing rate, whichever comes first.

Each task goes into the earliest scheduled input that starts at least 3 days and 5 FH before its deadline. Tasks of 10 man-hours or more (engine and module changes, gear changes, wiring troubleshooting) only go into a phase inspection.
Critical tasks, and tasks that are due now, go into an input that starts before the aircraft flies again. If none is scheduled, a before-next-flight input is opened on the as-of date.

If no scheduled input fits the deadline, a dedicated input is planned as late as the safety margin allows, and dedicated tasks on the same aircraft within 7 days are brought forward to share one input.
Man-hours come from the approved task card each recommendation cites (remove and install, inspection, troubleshooting, borescope, oil sampling), plus the phase and periodic servicing packages.

Deferral risk is the survival model's conditional failure probability for that unit over the FH until the next phase inspection, from the same fitted Weibull AFT parameters. Rule and trend items have no model risk.
Availability is the share of aircraft not in any planned input, averaged over each week. Unscheduled failures are not forecast here; the what-if planning screen covers expected unscheduled removals.
